items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: a guy that called Curtis Molesby. I guess you heard of him out there. He had nightclubs and everything after that, you know. Well, he take an O'Rell, and Wade Whaley to Frisco while I stayed in Los Angeles.

ctx.x: You mentioned then when you went to California, were there any other bands before you went out there, though, that you can tell us about that you played with?

No, I went out there with O'Rell. I didn't play with nobody but O'Rell. No, I didn't play with nobody but O'Rell. After the band broke up, well they raid the nightclubs, wherever that's so much, you know, and the bands broke up. And I got a job working for the railroad, working cleaning cars for the South Pacific a while. O'Rell, O'Rell, Wade, and Mutt, a guy taking them to Los Angeles, I don't know whether it was Los Angeles or Frisco, a guy that called Curtis Molesby. I guess you heard of him out there. He had…
I was waiting for the railroad there and got my job waiting for the railroad there. So you stayed out there there? A while.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: we got a job to go to Frisco with a drummer with me Curtis Molesby

ctx.x: And what kind of place was the cabaret? Cabaret. I clubbed his lap, just like Lee's.

And they closed him up at the same time, and they mixed dancing. But he listened at him, you know, see, he didn't get smart about him, they said. But they kept telling him not to do it, and he done it, but he just come and closed him up. He didn't have to close the place. Took his license. So after that, wasn't work around there. There wasn't nothing happening. So I went over to the Southern Pacific. They say they wanted some men to work over in the yard. Because I wasn't a man. I was a boy. I was 19 years old.…
